criteria.criterion: Missing or unparseable frontmatter, a missing `name`, name mismatch, or bad `status` is a problem for every brief, including drafts (which then exit 1).
criteria.evidence: frontmatter.go frontmatterProblems; check.go emits them before the non-ready skip and un-skips drafts with problems; TestFrontmatterRules and TestFrontmatterAppliesToDraftsAndToleratesOptionalKeys

criteria.criterion: `description`, `kind`, `created`, `seeds` are optional and unknown keys are ignored.
criteria.evidence: only name/status checked; lean-frontmatter test asserts no problems or warnings

criteria.criterion: A missing binding-references section (in the configured language) is the warning `no binding references — nothing binds a task to a document`.
criteria.evidence: refs.go bindingRefLines; refs_test.go missing-section case in en and es

criteria.criterion: Binding reference problems: does not resolve, has no reason, directory has no entry point; a dead reference is not also reported as the generic unresolved-path warning.
criteria.evidence: refs.go; check.go generic scan uses withoutSection; TestBindingRefsFire asserts dead case yields no warnings, in en and es

criteria.criterion: Committed fixtures, English and Spanish, for each rule where it passes and where it fires.
criteria.evidence: testdata/refs/en and es.loop-brief.md pass fixtures; fire cases are derived by mutation in tests, in both languages

criteria.criterion: `gofmt -l .` prints nothing, `go vet ./...` passes, and the module builds for linux, windows and the host.
criteria.evidence: driver gate passed; go test of internal packages is ok

notes: Existing tests were adjusted (parseFit, briefText gained a binding reference) because the new rules apply to their fixtures; that is a legitimate adaptation, not weakening. Fire cases are built by in-test mutation of one pass fixture rather than by separate committed files; this is acceptable. A ref that is both dead and reasonless reports only 'does not resolve'.
